newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarket efficiency hit by planners - report. [CORRECTED 15:08 GMT 15/10]
newsitem.headline: UK supermarket efficiency hit by planners - report. [CORRECTED 15:08 GMT 15/10]

text.p: (Corrects all references to sales per square metre to thousands of stg per square metre instead of stg/square metre)
British supermarkets could see their pre-eminence in the European efficiency stakes eroded by barriers to superstore development in the UK, a survey by research group Strategic Vision Ltd said.

"Their overall lead is being steadily reduced. The barriers to superstore development are putting this position at risk," a statement on the publication of the group's annual report on Europe's 75 largest grocery retailers said.
France's Monoprix currently tops the efficiency list with sales of 10,570 stg per square metre, the study shows.
But J. Sainsbury is second with 10,200 stg per square metre with Marks & Spencer following on 10,090 stg per square metre.
Britain has eight supermarkets of the top 25 European retailers in terms of sales per square foot, the report said, with ASDA and Tesco at sixth and seventh position respectively.
But French, Italian and Spanish retailers are challenging this position, Strategic Vision managing director James Ensor suggested in a statement.
"Faster development of giant hypermarkets in Spain and Italy will eventually threaten British dominance of the sales efficiency league," Ensor added.
British supermarkets face difficulties in gaining planning permission for large out-of-town stores as government guidelines currently promote alternative sites.
Ensor suggested that British supermarkets should try to expand in Europe instead of staying in the UK market.
Remaining in Britain "may be good for short-term profits but it puts at risk their long-term business expansion as the UK supermarket boom inevitably slows down," he said.
